items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Atstella and the pianist took the two rooms next door.

ctx.x: Our opening night was a big success and it was very joyful to be playing out in the open with the sky, the moon and stars above us. There was no canopy above the bandstand and the music did not go straight up to the sky, but I suppose Gabriel could hear what I was blowing. After our first set, I talked with some Italians that spoke english and were jazz fans and were happy to know they would have their favourite music to listen to for the first time in this resort.

After a few days, we started looking for a place where we could have a room and cook our own meals because we did not want to spend the biggest part of our small salary for hotel and restaurants expenses. Eventually, we found a place with a woman who had three rooms to rent and next door there were two rooms in a private home. Lily and I had a nice room in the front. Al Melili had a room alone, the drummer and bass shared a room. Atstella and the pianist took the two rooms next door. Fred Palmer of course had a…

Lily had volunteered to do the cooking for ourselves and the musicians that stayed in ourplace. We had two meals a day. After a few days the musicians started to ask for spaghetti at every meal before they ate anything else. Once or twice a week was enough for me and Lily. I started to get a little salty later when I realized that my woman was being a work horse for those guys that never offered her a small gift or a-nything, for what she was doing for them.
